name: Basilica of the Co-Cathedral of the Sacred Heart
history: Charleston was part of Virginia when the first priest visited in 1832. The parish built a small frame church in 1869. H. B. Lowe of Lexington, Kentucky, designed the present church, dedicated in December 1897. In 1974 it became co-cathedral of the Diocese of Wheeling-Charleston, and in 2009 a basilica.
arch: Romanesque Revival stone church with a single corner tower and spire.
features: A marble high altar and stained glass from Munich were installed in 1909.
Three bells were hung in 1911; the largest, St. Richard, weighs 2,600 pounds.

look.d: Its three bells of 1911 weigh from 700 to 2,600 pounds.
The windows came from Munich in 1909.

fun: The architect was paid $600 to design it.
journal: West Virginia's capital, a stone tower and Munich glass. Co-cathedral since 1974.

quiz.q: Where did the 1909 windows come from?
